draft.title: Buddhist sacred texts
card: Buddhism has no single holy book. Its teachings are kept in many collections of texts, called scriptures or sutras.
also called the Tipitaka, meaning three baskets. It is an early collection written in the Pali language and is the main scripture of the Theravada school.
Mahayana schools also value the early teachings, but they give great weight to later sutras, such as the Lotus Sutra and the Heart Sutra, written in Sanskrit and then translated.
So schools of Buddhism value different collections of texts, and no one collection is accepted by every school.
draft.remember: Buddhism has many scriptures, and each school values its own collections.

a.q: Which statement about Buddhist sacred texts is correct?
opts: Different schools value different collections of texts
All schools treat the Pali Canon as their only scripture
Buddhism has one holy book that all schools share
Only Theravada schools keep any written scriptures
a.why: Buddhism has many collections, and schools such as Theravada and Mahayana value different ones. The Pali Canon is central to Theravada, but Mahayana schools also value later sutras, so it is not the only scripture for all.
a.clue: Think about whether Buddhism has one book or many.

b.q: Dao belongs to a Mahayana community and studies the Heart Sutra. Which statement best explains why this text is not in the Pali Canon?
opts: Mahayana schools value later sutras as well as early texts
The Heart Sutra was written to replace the Pali Canon
Mahayana Buddhists reject all early Buddhist teachings
The Pali Canon holds only texts written in Sanskrit
b.why: Mahayana schools value later sutras such as the Heart Sutra alongside early teachings, so their collections differ from the Pali Canon. It is wrong that they reject the early teachings, because Mahayana schools also value them.
b.clue: Mahayana schools value more than one layer of texts.

a.best: Different schools value different collections of texts

b.best: Mahayana schools value later sutras as well as early texts

problems.detail: The clue 'Mahayana schools value more than one layer of texts' nearly restates the right option, so students can pick it without knowing the idea.

The stem asks why the Heart Sutra is not in the Pali Canon, but the right option only says what Mahayana schools value. The real reason is that the Heart Sutra is a later text, so the link is indirect and could confuse careful students.

b.q: Dao belongs to a Mahayana community and studies the Heart Sutra. Why is this text not found in the Pali Canon?
opts: It is a later sutra, not one of the early texts
It was written to replace the early Pali texts
Mahayana Buddhists reject the early teachings
The Pali Canon only holds texts in Sanskrit

problems.detail: Every wrong option uses an absolute word ('one', 'only', 'all ... only'), and the right option is the only hedged statement. A student could pick it without knowing the idea, and the clue ('one book or many') points straight to it.

The card says the collections are 'called scriptures or sutras'. Sutras (suttas) are only one kind of text. The Tipitaka also holds the Vinaya (monastic rules) and the Abhidhamma, so calling all the collections sutras is inaccurate.

'Each school values its own collections' suggests each school's texts are exclusive to it. The card says Mahayana schools also value the early teachings, so the line splits the schools more neatly than the card does.
